summary.headline: Gulshan Polyols H1 FY27 PAT rose 222% to INR92 crore and EBITDA margin hit 12.7%, but management flags Q3–Q4 margin pressure from record maize prices.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total income was INR614 crore (+13% YoY), EBITDA INR69 crore (+63%) at 11.2% margin, and PAT INR39 crore (+151%), driven by ethanol profitability. H1 FY27 EBITDA reached INR159 crore (+97%) at 12.7% margin, with PAT of INR92 crore. Management said record maize prices (INR30–32/kg) will pressure margins in Q3 and possibly Q4, but kept FY27 guidance unchanged. Debt fell to about INR233 crore from INR312 crore at FY26 end, and the company announced sorbitol and MDP/NDC expansions at Muzaffarnagar plus a green hydrogen BOO arrangement.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR427 crore with EBITDA INR62.5 crore (14.6% margin, vs 8.5% a year earlier). Company secured an allocation of 19.7 crore litres, with an order book of about INR1,300 crore plus about INR300 crore from by-products (about INR1,600 crore total).

segments.name: Grain processing
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR166 crore (+24% YoY) but EBITDA only INR2.45 crore (1.5% margin). Management attributes losses to the starch plant, which does not cover variable cost due to starch overcapacity in India.

segments.name: Mineral chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR22.7 crore and EBITDA INR4.6 crore (20.2% margin). On-site PCC slurry plant at Trident's Barnala site (22,000 tpa) is due April 2027, expected to add about INR20 crore revenue a year from FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: consolidated revenue about INR2,600 crore (ethanol INR1,700–1,800 crore, grain processing about INR800 crore, mineral about INR100 crore).
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin target of 10% and PAT margin about 5%.
Management said Q3 and possibly Q4 margins will be affected; ethanol margin guided at 11–12% for the full year. Consolidated EBITDA expected around 9–11%, and better than 10% as in FY26.
FY28 consolidated revenue target INR2,800–3,000 crore; management called the INR3,000 crore milestone achievable subject to execution and markets.
Ethanol volume: expects to execute about 22 crore litres by end of ESY 2026-27, with debottlenecking aimed at 24–25 crore litres.
capex_capacity: Sorbitol: new 30,000 tpa plant at Muzaffarnagar (UP), taking total sorbitol capacity to 1,10,000 tpa; aimed at North and Northeast India markets. Existing sorbitol capacity is in Gujarat (Bharuch).
MDP/NDC: expansion from 5,000 tpa to 30,000 tpa at Muzaffarnagar, flexible between maltodextrin powder and non-dairy creamer. Indicative mix about 20,000 t MDP and 10,000 t NDC.

Combined project cost about INR120 crore, funded about INR100 crore bank debt and about INR20 crore internal accruals. Commissioning targeted May 2027. Expected revenue INR200–250 crore at optimal levels (about 10–11% EBITDA margin); initial year INR120–130 crore; 2–3 year ramp-up.

Green hydrogen: ZFI to build, own and operate a 6 MW green hydrogen plant at the sorbitol facility under BOO model, with INR300 crore long-term contract over 10 years. Management expects about 20% cost saving versus open-market hydrogen and about 15,000 t annual CO2 reduction.
CWIP of about INR15 crore spread across Muzaffarnagar, Bharuch and Borgaon for ongoing capex. Management said the major ethanol investment phase is largely complete.
demand_pricing: Maize procurement prices are at record levels of INR30–32/kg, up from INR20–21/kg earlier. Management expects elevated prices for the next 2–3 months due to El Niño.
Ethanol becomes unviable above maize at INR26–27/kg; positive EBITDA is sustainable up to INR26/kg.

Feedstock allocation from OMCs: about 25% FCI rice, about 10% damaged food grains (DFG), and balance maize. Switching from maize to DFG/FCI rice takes 2–3 hours. OMCs save INR4–5 per litre on switching, and DDGS prices have provided a cushion.
Inventory rose about INR60 crore in the quarter as the company bought grain ahead of expected price moves and future grinding needs.
Country liquor (ENA) order of about INR100 crore for FY27 is tender-based and available once a year, with better margins than fuel ethanol. Selling prices: NDC about INR150/kg, MDP about INR50/kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current feedstock mix and how much of the shift to FCI rice and damaged grains is done?
qa_highlights.answer: Current allocation is about 25% FCI rice, 10% DFG and the balance maize. Management can request switches from maize to DFG when maize is not viable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the open market maize price, and will it moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize is INR30–32/kg, an all-time high. Industry is lobbying for an import duty cut. Management expects prices to stay elevated for the next 2–3 months.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors think about Q3 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margin pressure in Q3. H1 results give a cushion to meet full-year guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Muzaffarnagar expansion lift grain processing profitability, and how is it funded?
qa_highlights.answer: The expansion moves output away from starch, which is loss-making, toward sorbitol, MDP and NDC. Expected revenue is INR200–250 crore at about 10–11% EBITDA margin, funded about INR100 crore debt and INR20 crore internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per litre by feedstock, and can feedstock switches happen without restriction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-feedstock EBITDA changes daily and declined to give it, but reiterated 11–12% ethanol margin guidance. There are no technical bottlenecks to switching feedstock.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise about INR60 crore, and will it normalise in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory was built in advance of expected scarcity and rising prices to protect margins and cover future grinding. Management did not give a normalisation timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subsidy and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: A INR5 crore capital subsidy from Assam under NEIDS was netted against capex, not in P&L. Long-term debt is about INR123 crore (SBI INR103 crore, HSBC INR22 crore), with HSBC repaid by February 2027. A INR100 crore project loan sanction is expected in 2–3 quarters.

risks_watch: Maize at INR26–27/kg is the viability threshold for ethanol; Q3 and Q4 margins are expected to be pressured, and Q3 comparisons will be against a stronger base.
Working capital: the INR60 crore inventory build and any reversal could affect cash flow and debt.
Execution risk on the May 2027 Muzaffarnagar commissioning and the ramp-up over 2–3 years, plus the April 2027 Barnala PCC plant.
Green hydrogen plant (ZFI BOO, INR300 crore over 10 years) is a first-of-kind on-site set-up for the company and depends on the operator's delivery.
Policy: import duty on maize and OMC allocation rules; ethanol debottlenecking from 22 to 24–25 crore litres is not yet confirmed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 guidance and the H1 numbers, but cautious on near-term margins, which management said will be pressured by maize prices in Q3 and possibly Q4. Answers on feedstock EBITDA per litre were deflected as daily-varying, and the debt and subsidy answers were corrected on the spot.
key_quotes: Our full-year FY27 guidance remains unchanged.
We believe the INR3,000 crores revenue milestone is achievable, subject to execution and prevailing market conditions.
So, we are hoping to keep it around 9% to 11% maximum, not beyond that.
Maize prices are at an all-time high. The country has never seen these kinds of maize prices which they are seeing today.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Major ethanol investment phase is largely complete with CWIP only about INR15 crore, but a further INR100 crore project loan sanction is expected in 2-3 quarters and the company has just announced the sorbitol, MDP/NDC and green hydrogen projects, so further announcements are less certain.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance held at about INR2,600 crore and EBITDA margin guide was cut to 9-11% from a prior view, with H2 maize-driven margin pressure, so upside revisions look unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EBITDA margin guidance already trimmed to 9-11% and management flags Q3 and possibly Q4 pressure from maize at INR30-32/kg, above the INR26/kg ethanol viability threshold, with the ethanol margin guided at 11-12% for the full year.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The 30,000 tpa sorbitol plant and the MDP/NDC expansion (20,000 t MDP and 10,000 t NDC indicative mix) are slated for commissioning in May 2027, with initial-year revenue of INR120-130 crore.

rows.label: Starch plant losses under overcapacity
rows.why: Grain processing EBITDA only INR2.45 crore on INR166 crore revenue (1.5% margin) as the starch plant does not cover variable cost; the Muzaffarnagar shift away from starch is only commissioning in May 2027 with a 2-3 year ramp.

rows.label: Debt reduction and HSBC repayment
rows.why: Debt fell to about INR233 crore from INR312 crore at FY26 end and HSBC INR22 crore loan is due for repayment by February 2027, though a INR100 crore project loan sanction is expected in 2-3 quarters that would add back debt.
